clue.text: Where singers may make a splash in the Garden?

definitions.text: Where singers may make a splash in the Garden?

parts.words: Where singers may make a splash in the Garden?
parts.note: the singers are songbirds, and the splash is them bathing in a small water basin set out on a lawn, not a performance at Covent Garden opera house

explanation.surface: Opera singers making a big impression at Covent Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Garden' suggests Covent Garden, London's opera house, where singers make a splash by performing well; here it is just a back garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow basin in a garden where wild birds wash themselves is exactly a place where songbirds splash about.

clue.text: Player from an earlier time

definitions.meaning: a defender in football or rugby, positioned behind the forwards
dating from the past, as in old issues

explanation.definitionFit: A defensive footballer has this position name, and the adverb for a past date shares the spelling.

clue.text: Imprudent? A slice of bacon would be more so

definitions.text: A slice of bacon would be more so
definitions.meaning: the comparative of the word, with -er added, is also a slice of bacon

explanation.definitionFit: Hasty and reckless is the meaning, and its comparative form is a strip of bacon.

clue.text: Small block of cheese — what French Rechabite consumed

indicators.note: consumed means the cheese swallows the other pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese
que is French for what
a Rechabite is a teetotaller, TT; the Rechabites were a temperance society

explanation.surface: A small block of cheese and something a French teetotaller ate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rechabites were a nineteenth-century temperance society, so a member is a teetotaller; 'cheese' tempts as the definition, but 'Small block' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A compressed brick of coal dust or charcoal is a small block of fuel.

clue.text: Way to serve food, albeit raw at first

indicators.note: at first means the albeit and raw words come before the food word

parts.note: albeit means though, shortened to tho
raw means rough, unrefined
fare is food

explanation.surface: A way of serving food, even if it's raw to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to serve' only links the definition to the wordplay, and 'at first' sets the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public street is a way through a town.

clue.text: Not many following police over restriction on movement

indicators.note: following tells us the words for not many come after the police letters
over in a clue means turned over, so the police abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police force
not many means few

explanation.surface: Police impose a restriction because only a few people are out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Ulster Constabulary was the Northern Ireland police; 'over' turns its initials round to make CUR, and 'following' places the few after.
explanation.definitionFit: An order keeping people indoors during set hours is a legal limit on movement.

clue.text: Bones originally uncovered lying near archaeological excavation

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Bones found at an archaeological dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of 'uncovered lying near archaeological excavation'.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm bones on the little-finger side, in the plural, are bones.

clue.text: Sponger not occupied with computer program

parts.note: a vacant seat is free, not occupied
a loader is a program that loads software into memory

explanation.surface: An idle sponger with a computer program.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives off other people's generosity is a sponger.

clue.text: Irish writer first to catch Oriental antelope

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was an Irish writer

indicators.note: to catch means the word for first grabs the eastern letter inside it

parts.note: first means best, top
oriental means eastern, E

explanation.surface: An Irish writer is the first to catch an Asian antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts E inside BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu of African plains is a large antelope.

clue.text: Like the alibi of criminal kept out of a prison?

definitions.text: Like the alibi of criminal kept out of a prison?

parts.words: Like the alibi of criminal kept out of a prison?
parts.note: an alibi that kept a criminal out of jail must be unbreakable, and a prison may be built of a hard metal that is moulded in a foundry

explanation.surface: A criminal escapes jail thanks to an alibi nobody can break.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works two ways: an alibi solid enough to keep a criminal free, and a jail made out of moulded metal, as in iron bars.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbreakable, watertight alibi is described idiomatically with the name of a hard, rigid metal.

clue.text: Wind off drum, making fabulous noise

indicators.note: noise says the word for fabulous is to be heard, not read

parts.note: fabulous, as in incredible or fantastic, means unreal

explanation.surface: Someone winds something off a drum and makes an incredible noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noise' signals a soundalike: UNREAL said aloud gives the spelling of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind a line or film from a spool or drum is to take it off the reel.

clue.text: Set about sailor with characteristic restraint

indicators.note: about means the word set goes round the others

parts.note: taken as written
a trait is a characteristic
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is dealt with with typical restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb, but it is the outer piece taken as written; 'about' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas jacket that binds the arms is a restraint used on violent people.

clue.text: Unexpectedly lacking material to whiten the laundry?

definitions.meaning: suddenly, without warning, the sense of the idiom

definitions.text: lacking material to whiten the laundry?
definitions.meaning: laundry blue was a whitening agent added to the wash; to have none left is to have run out of it

explanation.surface: A household suddenly finds it has no whitener left for the washing.
explanation.walkthrough: Laundry blue (or 'blue bag') was a blue powder once added to rinse water to make white clothes look whiter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something happening with no warning, like a bolt from a clear sky, means unexpectedly.

clue.text: Fellow's supported by one old American like Basil, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the man's name sits above the others

parts.note: Herb is a man's name, a fellow; the 's stands for is
an ace is a one in cards
US is American

explanation.surface: A man named Basil propped up by an old American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' reads as a man's name, as in Basil Fawlty; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary plant, so plant-like or relating to such leafy plants describes it.

clue.text: Prejudice of one settled in political group

indicators.note: in means the one and settled words go inside the political group

parts.note: a party is a political group
I is one
settled, as a bird on a branch, means alit

explanation.surface: The bias of someone who has joined a political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' is in the past tense of alighting, the way a bird lands on a perch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias or favouritism towards one side is prejudice.

clue.text: One-time legal document correct in every detail

parts.note: one-time, as in former, is EX
an act is a law, a legal document passed by parliament

explanation.surface: A former legal document turns out to be accurate in every detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and accurate in each particular is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Saw lagers getting drunk in this?

definitions.text: Saw lagers getting drunk in this?

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are intoxicated, so they reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watching beers being consumed from drinking vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: SAW LAGERS rearranged ('drunk') gives the answer, and lagers are drunk from these items.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer glasses and tumblers are drinking vessels, the goods that lager is drunk from.

clue.text: Inducement to provide honey, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an inducement, such as a bribe
honey is an example of something that makes food sweet

explanation.definitionFit: A bribe is informally called by this name, and honey is an example of a sugar substitute.

clue.text: Creamy substance — complete food originally served in club

indicators.note: served in means the words before it are placed inside the club word

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball
complete, as in utter nonsense, means utter

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of food is used

explanation.surface: A rich creamy food served at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' sounds like a restaurant, but it places the pieces inside a club; 'originally' takes only the head of food.
explanation.definitionFit: The fatty part of milk from which butter is made is a creamy substance.

clue.text: Odds offered on race taking less than eleven seconds

indicators.note: taking less than the full words means only a run of letters inside eleven seconds is used

explanation.surface: Bookmakers offer odds on a sprint run in under eleven seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'elEVEN Seconds'. The surface suggests a sprint time.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money is the betting price where the stake is matched one to one, a price offered on a race.

clue.text: Wary about odd bits of their division's hire agreement

indicators.note: about means the word for wary goes round the other pieces

parts.note: wary means chary, cautious

indicators.note: odd bits means the first, third and fifth letters of their

parts.note: a division is a part; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Being cautious about some odd parts of a department's rental contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes TER from tHeIr, the letters in odd positions; a charter party is a shipping contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract for hiring a ship or aircraft is a hire agreement in shipping law.

clue.text: Educate attendants

definitions.meaning: to educate is to teach or coach
a retinue of attendants following a king

explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to teach them, and a monarch's retinue of followers shares the word.

clue.text: Put out, say, a small dog

indicators.note: say signals that the word for put out is heard, not read

parts.note: put out, as in annoyed, is piqued; pique means to annoy

explanation.surface: Turn out, for example, a little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a soundalike: PIQUE spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pekingese, a small Chinese toy breed, is shortened to this.

clue.text: A hiding-place for the port

parts.note: a den is a hiding-place or lair

explanation.surface: A hiding-place for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is a seaport in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaport city in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea is a port.

clue.text: Like an arch American soldier planted in ground in London

indicators.note: planted in means the soldier is placed inside the ground

parts.note: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier stationed at a London ground looks arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like 'roguish', but it is the noun. THE OVAL is a cricket ground in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed Gothic arch is an ogive, so the adjective describes that arch shape.

clue.text: Aggressive youth fell in front of van

indicators.note: in front of means the hide word is placed before the vanguard word

parts.note: fell is an animal's hide, a skin
van, short for vanguard, is the head of an army

explanation.surface: A youth falls in front of a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning animal hide; 'van' is the vanguard, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven-headed young thug of a youth subculture is an aggressive youth.

clue.text: Coming out with saw

definitions.meaning: coming out with words is uttering them
a saw is an old proverb or maxim

explanation.definitionFit: Uttering means speaking out, and a proverb is a well-known maxim; one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Hospital worker has little time to eat fish

indicators.note: to eat means the hospital worker takes the time abbreviation inside

parts.note: a surgeon works in a hospital
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A hospital worker has only a short time to eat some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts T inside SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bony-plated fish whose roe is caviar is a kind of fish.
